paper_sections.title: Promoter haplotypes of interleukin-10 gene linked to cortex plasticity in subjects with risk of Alzheimer's disease
Statistical analysis involving demographic and neuropsychological data

description.value: The study investigated whether interleukin-10 promoter ATA haplotype status was associated with hippocampal functional connectivity and cognition in amnestic mild cognitive impairment and healthy older adults.

design.value: A cross-sectional 2 × 2 design compared amnestic mild cognitive impairment subjects and healthy controls stratified by IL-10 promoter ATA haplotype status, using resting-state functional MRI and neuropsychological testing.

description.value: Delayed recall performance used to document objective memory impairment and evaluate episodic memory.
Cognitive functioning was evaluated using MMSE; aMCI subjects had an MMSE score of 24 or higher and controls had an MMSE score of 26 or higher.
The degree of dementia was determined using CDR.
Composite episodic-memory scores were calculated by averaging z-scores for auditory verbal learning test-delayed recall and Rey-Osterrieth complex figure test-delayed recall.
Composite scores were calculated from digit span, symbol digit modalities, trail-making test-A, trail-making test-B and clock-drawing test.

description.value: 39 aMCI subjects diagnosed according to Petersen et al. recommendations, including subjective and objective memory impairment, MMSE score of 24 or higher, CDR of 0.5, no or minimal impairment in activities of daily living, and absence of dementia.

description.value: Conventional axial T2-weighted anatomical images were obtained to rule out major white matter changes, cerebral infarction or other lesions; TR = 3500 ms; TE = 103 ms; flip angle = 90°; acquisition matrix = 320 × 192; FOV = 240 mm × 240 mm; thickness = 6.0 mm; gap = 0 mm; NEX = 2.0.

instrument.value: General Electric 1.5 Tesla scanner (General Electric Medical Systems, USA)

description.value: High-resolution T1-weighted axial images covering the whole brain were acquired using a 3D spoiled gradient echo sequence; TR = 9.9 ms; TE = 2.1 ms; flip angle = 15°; acquisition matrix = 256 × 192; FOV = 240 mm × 240 mm; thickness = 2.0 mm; gap = 0 mm.

instrument.value: General Electric 1.5 Tesla scanner (General Electric Medical Systems, USA)

description.value: 30 contiguous axial slices were acquired using a GRE-EPI pulse sequence; flip angle = 90°; acquisition matrix = 64 × 64; FOV = 240 × 240 mm; thickness = 4.0 mm; gap = 0 mm; 3.75 × 3.75 mm in-plane resolution parallel to the anterior commissure–posterior commissure line. This acquisition sequence generated 142 volumes in 7 min and 6 s.

The first eight volumes were discarded; remaining images were corrected for timing differences and motion effects, spatially normalized into the SPM5 Montreal Neurological Institute echo-planar imaging template with resampling to 3 × 3 × 3 mm voxels, smoothed with an 8 × 8 × 8 mm Gaussian kernel, detrended and temporally bandpass filtered at 0.01–0.08 Hz.

steps.value: The first eight volumes of the scanning session were discarded to allow for T1 equilibration effects.
The remaining images were corrected for timing differences and motion effects.
Participants with head motion of > 3 mm maximum displacement along any axis, or 3° of any type of angular motion were excluded.
The resulting images were spatially normalized into the SPM5 Montreal Neurological Institute echo-planar imaging template using default settings and resampling to 3 × 3 × 3 mm voxels.
The normalized images were smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 8 × 8 × 8 mm.
REST software was used to remove the linear trend of time courses and for temporal bandpass filtering (0.01–0.08 Hz).

model_settings.value: Cross-correlation between the mean time series of the bilateral hippocampal ROI and every voxel in the rest of the brain; Fisher's z-transform was applied; six head motion parameters and mean global, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals were introduced as covariates; voxelwise-based grey matter volume correction was applied.

level.value: subject-level maps followed by group-level analysis

estimator.value: cross-correlation analysis followed by Fisher's z-transform

model_settings.value: 2 × 2 ANOVA: groups × haplotypes; groups: aMCI and controls; haplotypes: without ATA haplotype and with ATA haplotype. Corrected p < 0.05 by Monte Carlo simulation, single voxel p = 0.05, minimum cluster size 10,503 mm3, FWHM = 8 mm, with mask.

estimator.value: Monte Carlo simulation for multiple comparisons

model_type.value: independent-samples t-test and Pearson correlative analysis

model_settings.value: Mean functional connectivity within the mask of ANOVA interactions was extracted from each subject's image; independent-samples t-tests were used for group comparisons and correlations were performed between neuropsychological test scores and mean functional connectivity.
